answer.label: Recommend (ii): never auto-release on intake rejection. `absent` proves no campaign-ledger intake root, but not that the post-claim rejection was unavoidable or that this run owns the mismatched claim. A no-effect release marks claim A released/terminal, resets its graph node to pending, and excludes released claims from consumed gate-attempt counting; attempt N+1 can therefore be minted, recreating the “burns a grant” retry path. Protect against deterministic bad inputs or binding drift repeatedly advancing attempts without operator acknowledgment. The RED test should pin that `mission_grant_ref_mismatch` plus `resolution: absent` emits `stranded_claim` and exact recovery, creates no `no_effect_release`, leaves claim A live with its reservation and active node binding, and makes the next grant fail `attempt_blocked_by_open_claim`; only explicit withdraw/terminalization may clear A and permit the next attempt. No rejection-code allowlist is justified by the supplied artifacts.
